notes:
Maintainer risk: HIGH — stale documentation says NC is not implemented (security misrepresentation), DN excluded subtrees are silently not enforced for 8 PKITS cases, and anchor-supplied initial NC state is never applied per RFC 5280 §6.1.1.
Confidence: 25% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: PKIX-vjc.3 (DN excluded subtree direction — the actual test failure cause needs verification by running the test with debug output; I inferred the direction from PKITS expected results but could be wrong about which direction is correct). PKIX-vjc.5 (test 30 ignore comment may be stale — the arithmetic looks like it should pass; may be failing for unrelated reason). Uncertainty driven by: cannot run the tests in this review pass, and x509_cert::ext::pkix::constraints::name::GeneralSubtrees API (push/extend methods, as_slice) assumed from usage patterns not verified. Would raise confidence if: I could run cargo test and get the actual failure output for tests 7, 30.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — no unsafe, no unwrap outside tests, non_exhaustive on Error, #[forbid(unsafe_code)]. The main idiom issues are &Option<T> instead of Option<&T> (PKIX-vjc.23), an avoidable clone (PKIX-vjc.24), and a bool parameter where an enum would read better (PKIX-vjc.25). None are show-stoppers.
Rust idiom confidence: 15% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: PKIX-vjc.24 (the clone may be unavoidable given x509_cert GeneralName ownership structure — haven't checked if GeneralName::DirectoryName can take a &Name reference). Uncertainty driven by: did not inspect x509_cert::ext::pkix::name::GeneralName definition to confirm whether a borrow-based construction is possible.
title: Review: NameConstraints RFC 5280 §4.2.1.10 implementation
